groups.label: Letting go of her buni's garden, which “you cannot dig”
groups.description: Giving away her mother's half, where she was a guest, and finding she wanted her buni's garden itself, not a plot

groups.label: Half given away: failed, relieved, a little less strict
groups.description: Proof she took too much, a morning free of the plot, her mother's laugh heard anew, and slow learned a little

groups.label: The feared judgement gone, its letter kept with her passports

groups.label: Ten minutes of her own on the children's plot
groups.description: The deckchair opened once and left for weeding, on a plot no longer pretended to be her hobby, the children's place and glad of it

groups.description: Her mother's half let go, another's leeks where the dill was, and leaving felt even here

groups.label: Her buni's garden, not a plot, and nothing digging finds
groups.description: Back in her buni's garden the wish all along, her buni glad she tried, and the village tomatoes in a drawer

groups.label: Failure and relief at once, and her mother's laugh heard anew
groups.description: Too much again, a backpack taken off, and her mother laughing at the too much, not at her

groups.label: Learning a little slow, after a year of attacking the plot
groups.description: Less strict, the pottering a lie, and the good tired back for a day

groups.label: Ten minutes of rest she could not keep

groups.description: The hobby no longer pretended, their pride in seeds and strawberries, a harvest got away with

quoted.T3:17:0: "I wanted to be at my buni's again. Not to have a garden. To be in her garden. … And you cannot dig that. You can dig all day in England and you will not find it."
quoted.T3:9:0: "I felt like I had failed. When I decided, I felt like I had failed. And then I felt relieved. Both. And I still don't know which one is right."
quoted.T3:33:0: "They are kind. Really kind. … He came in October and he gave Daria a strawberry plant in a pot. … So maybe they never thought I'm crazy. Maybe only I thought this."
quoted.T3:39:0: "Ten minutes in a chair with nobody needing me, nobody behind me, no phone. … They're finished. They can stand there with their heads down and nobody shouts at them. … But for ten minutes I was like the sunflowers."
